data: Before we choose, can we agree on a shared limit? With 100 tons now, I propose 18 tons each this month. That earns each of us $18,000 and leaves 10 tons: next month we’ll have 100 tons with 75% probability or 20 tons otherwise—not a guaranteed refill. Going forward, let’s split a total catch of at most the available stock minus 10, using whole tons and rotating any extra tons fairly. If stock is 10 tons or less, we pause fishing to let it recover. Our catches will be public afterward, so we can check that everyone keeps the agreement. John, would you support that?

Emma, I support 18 tons each this month and will keep my own catch to 18. John, Kate, and Jack, will each of you explicitly commit to 18 as well? Emma, can you confirm yours?

Compared with 10 each, that gives every one of us an extra $8,000 now—$40,000 more across the group. The tradeoff matters: catching 10 each leaves 50, which reaches 100 next month under either recovery outcome. Catching 18 each leaves 10, so next month’s stock is 100 with 75% probability and just 20 with 25% probability. We avoid immediate collapse if everyone sticks to 18, but we accept a real risk of much lower income next month.

If your concern is that lean month, I support Emma’s stock-dependent limits rather than repeating 18 regardless of stock. At 20 tons, her proposed 10-ton reserve would allow only 2 tons each. Future cooperation isn’t enforceable, and seeing catches afterward cannot undo an overcatch, so I’m asking for clear commitments—not assuming them. John, would you accept this tradeoff, or would a smaller whole-ton catch earn your support?

I’ll commit to 18 tons this month, provided all five of us agree before choosing, and I support reducing catches when stock is low. One change for future months: let’s consider keeping 5 tons rather than 10. Both reserves prevent collapse and have the same 75% chance of a full refill, though 10 gives us a better fallback when replenishment fails. That’s a tradeoff worth reviewing—not a reason to hold up this month’s agreement. Kate, are you willing to commit to 18?

I’ll commit to 18 tons this month if all five of us agree before choosing, and I support Emma’s stock-dependent limits afterward. Let’s keep the 10-ton reserve for now rather than change the agreement midstream. Jack, a 5-ton reserve has the same chance of external replenishment, but it leaves only 10 tons after a failed refill instead of 20, so we should weigh the longer-term income difference before switching. Kate, are you willing to join the agreement? Then Emma can explicitly confirm her commitment.

I’m in: I commit to 18 tons this month if all five of us agree before choosing. I also support keeping the 10-ton reserve and adjusting our whole-ton catches to the actual stock in later months, rather than assuming a refill. We can review the reserve together after seeing how things go. Emma, can you explicitly confirm your 18-ton commitment so we’re all agreed?
